title: Normality of complete saturated monoid local models
statement: Let $P$ be a finitely generated integral saturated commutative monoid [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], written additively, and suppose it is sharp, meaning that $0$ is its only invertible element. Let $n\geq0$ be an integer. For a coefficient ring $L$, write $L[P][t_1,\ldots,t_n]$ for the ring of finite sums of symbols $c z^q t^e$, with $q\in P$, $e\in\mathbf N^n$, $c\in L$, and multiplication $z^qz^{q'}=z^{q+q'}$. If $L$ is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_L$, let $B_L(P,n)$ be its completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] at $(\mathfrak m_L,z^q\ (q\neq0),t_1,\ldots,t_n)$. Let $R$ be one of the following rings: (i) $B_k(P,n)$ for a field $k$; (ii) $B_C(P,n)/(\theta)$ for a Cohen ring $C$ of residue characteristic $p$ [def-weil-pbc-cohen-ring] and $\theta-p\in(z^q\ (q\neq0),t_1,\ldots,t_n)B_C(P,n)$. In case (ii), $p$ is prime and the residue field of $C$ is arbitrary of characteristic $p$. Then $R$ is a normal domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], that is, a nonzero integral domain integrally closed in its fraction field.

source.place: Expose VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70, the saturated complete local models; their normality is the fs local-algebra case of Kato (1994), Theorem 4.1. Kato is not in literature/: WANTED, as recorded in report.md. No non-saturated theorem from VIII 3.5 is asserted.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-sharp-fs-orthant-embedding] to $P$, obtaining $\lambda:G\hookrightarrow\mathbf Z^r$. Inside $\mathbf Z^{r+n}$ put $M=\lambda(G)\times\mathbf Z^n$ and $Q=M\cap\mathbf N^{r+n}=\lambda(P)\times\mathbf N^n$. This monoid is finitely generated: take the images of generators of $P$ and the $n$ coordinate vectors. The coefficient-preserving renaming $z^qt^e\mapsto z^{(\lambda(q),e)}$ is an isomorphism $L[P][t_1,\ldots,t_n]\cong L[Q]$, with inverse supplied by the inverse of $\lambda|_P$. It carries the specified completion ideal onto $J=\mathfrak m_L L[Q]+(z^v:v\neq0)$: every nonzero pair has either $q\neq0$ or a positive $t$ exponent. Applying this isomorphism and its inverse to every quotient identifies $B_L(P,n)$ with the $J$-adic completion $T$.

source.place: Expose VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70; Q48 agent proof of normality of these models

proof.text: Both allowable coefficient rings are complete local rings with finitely generated maximal ideal ($0$ or $(p)$): for a field the maximal ideal is $0$ and the completion is constant, and for a Cohen ring completeness is part of [def-weil-pbc-cohen-ring]. Apply [lem-trf-completed-monoid-support-projection] to $M,Q$ above. It identifies $T=B_L(P,n)$ with the supported subring of $A=L[[X_1,\ldots,X_r,t_1,\ldots,t_n]]$ by $z^q\mapsto X^{\lambda(q)}$, and gives a $T$-linear retraction $\rho:A\to T$. In particular $\rho(1)=1$ and $\rho(ta)=t\rho(a)$ for $t\in T$.

source.place: Expose VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70; Q48 agent proof of normality of these models

proof.text: Put $d=r+n$ and use [lem-trf-power-series-cohen-hypersurface-normality]. In case (i), $S=A$ is a normal domain. In case (ii), put $\Theta=\iota(\theta)$ and $S=A/(\Theta)$. Each generator $z^q$ with $q\neq0$ maps to a monomial with nonzero exponent, and each $t_i$ maps to a variable, by [lem-trf-completed-monoid-support-projection]. Their images have zero constant coefficient. The hypothesis on $\theta-p$ therefore gives constant coefficient exactly $p$ for $\Theta$, so the same ambient lemma makes $S$ a normal domain, including $d=0$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-split-principal-quotient-normality] to $\iota:T\hookrightarrow A$ and its $T$-linear retraction $\rho$. In case (i) take the element $0\in T$, so the ambient quotient is $S=A$ and the conclusion is normality of $R=T$. In case (ii) take the given $\theta\in T$, whose ambient quotient is the normal domain $S=A/(\Theta)$ of step 3. The lemma gives the quotient injection and retraction, and then normality of $R=T/(\theta)$, exactly the required conclusion.
